x: We have previously explained his saying: Ha Meem in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

And His statement: And the clear Book is an oath from God Almighty. He swears by this Book that He revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: And the clear Book for whoever ponders it and thinks about its lessons and sermons, it will guide him, direct him, and provide evidence of its truth, and that it is a revelation from a Wise, Praiseworthy One, not an invention by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor a fabrication by anyone.

Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an. He says: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an in the language of the Arabs, since you, O those warned by it from the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were Arabs. That you may understand. He says: So that you may understand its meanings and the admonitions it contains. He did not send it down in the language of the non-Arabs, making it foreign, so that you would say: We are Arabs, and this is foreign speech whose meanings we do not understand. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: “Ha Meem. By the clear Book” is this clear Book.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Ha Meem. By the clear Book.” Clear, and God is its blessing, guidance, and right direction.

x: God Almighty says: And indeed, this Book is the original Book from which this Book was copied, with Us. It is exalted: He says: Of loftiness and elevation, Wise: Its verses have been perfected, then explained in detail, so it is full of wisdom. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Yaʿqub told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawaʿi, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, he said: ʿUrwah ibn ʿAmir told us, that
m: he heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what He wanted to create. He said: And the book is with Him. He said: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, sublime and wise.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Atiyah bin Sa’d, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, sublime and wise, meaning the Qur’an in the Mother of the Book from which God has abrogated.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard Malik narrating on the authority of Imran, on the authority of Ikrimah,
h
And it is in the Mother of the Book with Us
. He said: The Mother of the Book is the Qur’an.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is in the Mother of the Book with Us
. He said: The Mother of the Book is the root of the Book and its entirety.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And it is in the Mother of the Book: meaning the entirety of the Book, meaning the origin of the Book.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And it is in the Mother of the Book. He said: In the book that is with God in the original. And his saying: With us is the Most High, the Wise, and we have already mentioned its meaning. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: With us is Ali, a wise man, informing us of his status, virtue, and honor.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: Shall we turn away from you and leave you, O polytheists, as you think, and not remind you of our punishment because you are a people of polytheists.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
Shall We turn away from you the Reminder
? He said: You deny the Qur’an and then you are not punished for it.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Shall We turn away from you the Reminder
? He said: With punishment.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: h
Shall We turn away from you the Reminder
? He said: Shall We turn away the punishment from you?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Shall We turn away from you the Reminder
because you were a transgressing people? He said: Do you think that We will turn away from you while you have not done what you were commanded to do?

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Should we abandon reminding you of this Qur’an and not remind you of it, because you are a transgressing people?
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Shall We turn away from you the Reminder

because you are a transgressing people?: meaning, polytheists. By God, if this Qur’an had been lifted when the first of this nation rejected it, they would have perished. So he called them to it for twenty years, or as long as God willed.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Should We turn away from you the Reminder

? He said: If this nation did not believe, the Reminder would be turned away from them. He said: The Reminder is what was revealed to them of what God commanded them to do and forbade them, turning away from it, not mentioning anything of it to you. The more correct interpretation of this is the interpretation of those who interpreted it: Shall We then avert the punishment from you and leave you and turn away from you, because you were a transgressing people who did not believe in your Lord? We said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse, because God Almighty followed that with His report about the nations that came before the nations that He threatened with this verse, regarding their denial of His messengers, and the punishment that He brought upon them. In that is evidence that His statement,
h
Should We turn away from you the message

? is a warning from Him to those addressed by it from the polytheists, since they followed in their denial of what came to them from God, their Messenger, the same path as those who came before them. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it as <in kuntum>with a kasra on the alif of <in>, meaning: Should We then turn away from you the Reminder, since you were a transgressing people?

x: Some of the reciters of Mecca and Kufa, and the majority of the reciters of Basra, recited it as <an>with a fatha on the alif of <an>, meaning: because you were. The Arabists differed about the reason for the opening of the alif in an in this position.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was opened because the meaning of the sentence is: because you were.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Whoever opens it is as if he intended something in the past tense. He said: And you say in the sentence: I came that you forbade me, meaning: when you forbade me. And it is broken if you meant: I came that you would forbid me. And similar to it is: Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from turning away from you and that they turned away from you
r
(Al-Ma’idah 5:6)

with a broken and a fathah. Perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, if they do not believe in this message. (al-Kahf 18:6) He said: The Arabs recite the words of Al-Farazdaq: Are you upset that Qutaybah's ears were cut openly and you did not feel upset about the killing of Ibn Hazim? He said: And he recites: I am afraid that the deposited mixture and the pure rope of Azza’s broken rope have become clear He said: In each of the two verses there is what is in the other of kasra and fatha.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it as <in kuntum>with a kasra on the alif of <in>, meaning: Should We then turn away from you the Reminder, since you were a transgressing people?
Some of the reciters of Mecca and Kufa, and the majority of the reciters of Basra, recited it as <an>with a fatha on the alif of <an>, meaning: because you were.

x: God Almighty says: And how many prophets have We sent O Muhammad, in the first generations that passed before the generation in which you were sent, just as We sent you among your people from Quraysh.

And there never came to them a prophet but they used to ridicule him. He says: And there never came to a generation of those generations or a nation of those nations before us a prophet calling them to guidance and the path of truth, but those to whom that prophet came from among those nations, whom he sent to them, used to ridicule them, just as your people ridicule you, O Muhammad. He says: So do not let what your people do to you be too great for you, and do not let them be distressed by it, for in their mockery of you they only followed the path of their forefathers and the way of their past imams from among the disbelievers in God.

God Almighty says: So We destroyed those who were more severe in their violence than those who mocked their prophets when they attacked. But they did not outstrip Us with their strength and the severity of their violence, nor were they able to resist Our punishment when it came to them. So those who are weaker than them in strength are more likely to be unable to resist Our punishment when it befalls them. And
h
the example of the former peoples

has passed. God Almighty says: And the example of those who mocked you and those before them of their likes has passed for us, which We represented to them in their likes from among those who denied Our messengers whom We destroyed. He says: So let those who mock you, O Muhammad, expect from Our punishment the same as that which We brought upon those who persisted in denying you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And the example of the former ones has passed away, he said: The punishment of the former ones.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
The example of the former peoples
, he said: Their way.

x: God Almighty says: And if you ask, O Muhammad, these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:Who created the seven heavens and the earths, and brought them into existence and originated? They will say: The Almighty created them in His power and in His vengeance against His enemies, the All-Knowing of them and of what is in them. Nothing is hidden from Him.

Who made the earth a cradle for you means: He who made the earth a bed for you, so that you may tread it with your feet and walk upon it with your legs. And made for you therein paths means: He made easy for you roads therein that you may take from one town to another, for your livelihood and your trade.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And He made for you therein paths meaning roads.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Who has made the earth a bed for you He said: A carpet. And has made for you therein paths He said: The roads. That you may be guided He says: So that you may be guided by those paths to wherever you want of countries, villages, and cities. Were it not for that, you would not be able to endure the spaciousness of your courtyards and homes, but it is a blessing that He has bestowed upon you.

x: God the Most High says: And He who sent down from the sky water in due measure. Meaning, whatever rain He sent down from the sky in due measure: He says: according to your need for it. So He did not make it like a flood, so that it would be a punishment like that which He sent down upon the people of Noah, nor did He make it little, so that plants and crops would not grow because of its scarcity. Rather, He made it a soothing rain, and a revival of the dead land, bringing it to life. Then We revived thereby a dead land. Allāh the Most High says: Then We revived thereby a dead land from among your lands, meaning barren, with no plants or crops in it, destroyed by barrenness and rotted by drought. Thus will you emerge. Allāh the Most High says: Just as We brought forth, by this water that We sent down from the sky, plants and crops from this dead land after its barrenness and drought, thus, O people, you emerge, after your annihilation and destination in the earth, as remains, by the water that He sent down to it to revive you from it after your death, alive as you were before your death.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And He who sends down water from the sky in due measure… the verse, just as God revived this dead earth with this water, likewise you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection. And it was said: We were resurrected by it, because its meaning is: We were revived by it. And if the earth was described as being revived, it would be said: The earth was resurrected, as Al-A’sha said: Until people say from what they saw, Oh, how strange is the dead man who spreads the report.

x: And His statement:
h
And He Who created all pairs

means, the Most High says: And He Who created everything and paired it, meaning He created the males from the females in pairs, and the females from the males in pairs. And He made for you from the ships which are the ships and the livestock which are the beasts that which you ride meaning: He made for you from the ships what you ride in the seas to wherever you intend and rely in your travel in them for your livelihoods and your needs, and from the livestock what you ride on land to wherever you want in the countries, such as camels, horses, mules, and donkeys.

God Almighty says: So that you may be firmly established on the backs of what you ride. Arabic grammarians differed about the reason for the singularization of the ha’ in the phrase on his backs and its masculinization.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its masculinization refers to what you ride, and what is masculine, as one says: I have women who suit you and please you. Cattle may be made masculine or feminine. And He said in another place:
from what is in their bellies
and in another place: their bellies
r
(An-Nahl 16:60)

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The backs were added to the singular because the singular is in the sense of a plural like the soldiers and the army. It was said: Why didn’t you say: so that you may mount on his back, making the back one when you add it to one? I said: The singular has the meaning of a plural, so you returned the back to the meaning, and did not say his back, so it is like the singular whose meaning and pronunciation are the same. Similarly, you say: The women of the soldiers have multiplied, and you say: And the soldiers raised their eyes and did not say his eye. He said: And likewise, all the nouns that are described are added to it, so make them difficult to pluralize them. And if a noun is added to it in the meaning of a verb, it is permissible to make it plural or singular, like your saying: The army raised its voice, and its voices are better. And this is permissible because the verb has no form in two except its form in one.

Another of them said: It was said: So that you may be established on their backs, because it is a description of the heavens, but he made the ha’ singular, because heaven is interpreted as a plural, so he made the backs plural and made the ha’ singular, because the verbs of each one whose interpretation is the plural are singular and plural like: the army is defeated and defeated, so if the names come and nothing else, then you say: the army is men, therefore he made the backs plural and made the ha’ singular, and if it was like the voice and similar things, it would be permissible for the army to raise its voice and its voices. His statement:
h
Then remember the favor of your Lord God Almighty says

: Then remember the favor of your Lord which He bestowed upon you by making it subject to you as mounts on land and sea when you are seated thereon so that you glorify and extol Him, and say, Glory be to God who made subject to us this ship and livestock that we have ridden, from what the polytheists describe Him with, and associate with Him in worship of idols and statues, and we could not have subdued it.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Kurayb and Ubayd ibn Ismail al-Hibari narrated to us:

c: Al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, who said:
m: I rode an animal and said: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have subdued it. A man from the people of the house heard me - Abu Kurayb and al-Hibari said - al-Maharibi said: I heard Sufyan say: He is al-Hasan ibn Ali, may God be pleased with them both - and he said: Is this what you have been commanded to do? He said: Say: Praise be to God who has guided us to Islam, praise be to God who has blessed us with Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, praise be to God who has made us among the best nation produced for mankind. So you have mentioned great blessings, then you say after that: “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: that al-Hasan ibn Ali, may God be pleased with him, saw a man riding an animal, and he said: Praise be to God who has subjected this to us, and then he mentioned something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: That you may mount on their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you are mounted on them. He teaches you what to say when you embark on a ship. You say, “In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.”
r

, and when you mount camels, you say, “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return.” And He teaches you what to say when you dismount from the mountains and the livestock altogether. You say, O God, let us descend at a blessed landing place, and You are the best of those who grant landing places.

x: And His saying: And indeed, to our Lord we will return. God Almighty says: And that they may also say: And indeed, to our Lord, after our death, we will return to Him.

God Almighty says: These polytheists have given God a share of His creation, and that is because they say to the angels: They are the daughters of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And they assigned to Him from among His servants a portion, he said: Sons and daughters from the angels.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they assigned to Him a portion of His servants
. He said: The daughters.

x: Others said: What is meant by the part here is: justice.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they assigned to Him a portion of His servants
: meaning, equal.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And they assigned to Him a portion of His servants

: meaning, equal. We chose the statement we chose in interpreting that because God, the Most High, followed that with His statement: Or has He taken from among those He creates daughters and preferred you with sons? as a rebuke to them for what you said. So it was known that His rebuke to them with that was only for what He reported about what they said about attributing daughters to God, the Most High. And His statement: Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful. God Almighty says: Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful for the favors of his Lord which He has bestowed upon him. He says: He makes his ingratitude for His favors upon him clear, to whoever contemplates it with the thought of his heart and ponders his situation.

x: And His statement:
h
Or has He taken from what He creates daughters

? God Almighty says, rebuking these polytheists who described Him as saying that the angels are His daughters: O ignorant ones, has your Lord taken from what He creates daughters, while you are not satisfied for yourselves? And He has chosen you with sons. He says: And He has chosen you with sons, so He made them for you.

And if one of them is given good report of what is given as an example for the Most Merciful, God Almighty says: And if one of these polytheists who make a part of God's servants a part of what is given as an example for the Most Merciful, he says: What is given as an example for God, so he likens Him to a likeness, and that is what He described Him with, that He has daughters.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
By what He has set forth as an example for the Most Merciful
, he said: A son.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
By what He has given an example of the Most Merciful is by what He has given to God
. And His statement:
h
His face remained blackened means that God Almighty says

: The face of this one who was given the good report of what the Most Merciful had given him as an example of daughters remained blackened from the evil of what he had been given the good report of. And he was filled with inward grief means that he was sad.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: and he is filled with grief: meaning sad.

x: God Almighty says: Or one who plants ornaments and adorns himself with them while he is in dispute meaning: while he is in dispute with the one who disputes with him during the dispute without making clear what he said, and with the one who disputes with him with proof and argument, due to his inability and weakness. You made him a part of God’s creation and you claimed that he is his share of them. And in the speech there is something omitted that is sufficient with the evidence of what was mentioned from it, which is what I mentioned. The commentators differed on the meaning of his statement:
h
Or one who grows up in adornment and is not clear in dispute
Some of them said: By that he meant female slaves and women.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
Or one who grows up in adornment and is in dispute not clear
he said: He means the woman.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Marthad, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Women were permitted to wear silk and gold, and he recited: Or one who grows up in adornment while in dispute he is not clear. He said: He means the woman.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Or one who grows up in adornment and is in dispute not clear
, he said: The female slaves you have attributed to the Most Merciful as children. How do you judge?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Or one who grows up in finery and is in dispute not clear, he said: The female slaves he fools with that, not clear of their weakness.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Or one who grows up in adornment, meaning: They gave him daughters, and when one of them is given the good report of them, his face darkens, and he is filled with inward grief. He said: As for his statement, and he is not clear in dispute, he means: rarely does a woman speak and want to present her argument except that she is presented with an argument against herself.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Or one who grows up in adornment and is not clear in dispute
. He said: An-Nisa.

x: Others said: He meant by that their idols that they worshipped instead of God.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Or one who is raised in ornaments… the verse, he said: These are their statues that they make of silver and gold, which they worship. They are the ones who created them, they made them from that ornament, then they worshipped them. And he is in the dispute, not clear. He said: He does not speak, and he recited: Then he is a clear opponent.
r

The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who say: What is meant by that are female slaves and women, because that follows God’s statement about the polytheists’ attributing to Him what they dislike for themselves of daughters, and their lack of knowledge of His right, and their adorning Him with attributes and miserliness – while He is their Creator, Owner, Provider, and Bestower of blessings upon them which He enumerated at the beginning of this surah – which they would not like for themselves. So following that speech with something similar to it is more appropriate and more fitting than following it with something that is not mentioned. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: Or whoever grows up in adornment. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Meccans and Kufians, read it as or whoever grows up with a fatha on the yaa and a light stress on the yaa from nasha’a yansha’. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as yansha’ with a damma on the yaa and a shaddah on the shin from nasha’tuhu, so he is yansha’. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning, because the origin of the construction is nashe’, and the originating is originated, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, it is or from whom they create except in adornment al-hilya. In from there are several grammatical aspects: the nominative case as a resumption and the accusative case as an omission of they make yaddu’lu as if it were said: or from whom

They meant Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, who was called the flower of Quraish. This one was from Mecca, and Mas’ud bin Amr bin Ubaidullah Al-Thaqafi was from the people of Taif. He said: God Almighty says in response to them: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? I do what I want. And His statement:
h
We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world

, meaning, the Most High says: Rather, We apportion Our mercy and honor among whom We will of Our creation. We make whom We will a messenger, and whom We will a friend, and We take whom We will as a close friend, just as We apportioned among them their livelihood by which they live in their life of this world of provisions and sustenance. We made some of them higher in degree than others, rather We made this one rich, and this one poor, this one a king, and this one a slave, so that some of them may take others in servitude. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: Do they divide the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world. So he met him weak-willed and feeble-tongued, though he had been given abundant provision. And he met him strong-willed and sharp-tongued, though he was oppressed. God, the Most High, said:
h
We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world
, just as He had apportioned among them their forms and their morals, blessed and exalted be our Lord. And His statement:
h
So that some of them may make use of others in mockery

means: So that this one may make use of that one in his service to him, and in the return of this one to that one with what he has of bounty in his hands. He says: God Almighty made the mention of some for others a cause of livelihood in this world.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding what was meant by his saying:
h
So that some of them may take others in mockery
Some of them said: Its meaning is what we said about it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So that some of them may take others in mockery
, he said: Some of them may use others in mockery.

x: God Almighty says: And had it not been that mankind would have become one community: one group. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of why they would not have been assured of their unanimity in it, had He done what He, the Most High, said, and what He did not do for His sake.

Some of them said, that is their unanimity in disbelief. He said, the meaning of the statement is: And were it not that mankind would be one community in disbelief, and all of them would become disbelievers, We would have made
h
for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful
roofs of silver for their houses.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And had it not been that mankind would be one community
, God Almighty says: Had it not been that I would make all mankind disbelievers, I would have made the disbelievers’ houses have roofs of silver.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Hudhahah ibn Khalifa told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And had it not been that mankind would be one community

, he said: Had it not been that mankind would all be disbelievers, inclined towards the world, God, the Blessed and Exalted, would have made what He said. Then he said: By God, the world has inclined towards most of its people, and He did not do that, so how would it have been if He had done that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And had it not been that mankind would be one community
: meaning all of them would be disbelievers.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And had it not been that mankind would be one community
, he said: had it not been that people would be disbelievers.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And had it not been that mankind would be one community
, meaning: disbelievers of one religion.

x: Others said: Their gathering to seek this world and abandon seeking the Hereafter. He said: The meaning of the words is: If only people would be one nation seeking this world and rejecting the Hereafter.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And had it not been that mankind would be one community
, he said: Had it not been that people would choose their worldly life over their religion, We would have made this for the people of disbelief. And His statement:
h
For those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful
, We would have made roofs of silver for their houses. God Almighty says:
h
For those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful
in this world, We would have made roofs, meaning the tops of their houses, of silver.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: For their houses, a roof of silver. The roof: the top of the houses. The Arabists differed about the repetition of the lam in His statement: For those who disbelieve and in His statement: For their homes.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra claimed that it was inserted into the homes as a substitute.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: If you wish, you can make it repeated in for their homes, as in They ask you about the sacred month of fighting therein
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:217)

. Or if you wish, you can make the two lams different, as if the second one is in the meaning of on, as if he said: We made a roof for them over their homes. He said: The Arabs say to a man to his face: I made gifts for you for your people, meaning I made them for them on your behalf. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement: <a roof>. The majority of the reciters of Mecca, some of the Medinans, and the majority of the Basrans read it as <a roof>with a fat-ha on the seen and a sukoon on the qaf, considering that to be in accordance with His statement: Then the roof fell upon them from above them (al-Nahl 16:26) and explaining that to the fact that it has one wording and means the plural.

Some of the reciters of Medina and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as <a roof>with a damma on the seen and the qaf, explaining that it is the plural of saqifa or saquf. If it is explained that it is the plural of saquf, then it is the plural of the plural, because saquf is the plural of saqf, then the saqf are pluralized as saqf, so that is similar to the reading of those who read it as <a pledge held>(al-Baqarah 2:283) with a damma on the ra’ and the ha’, which is the plural, and its singular is rihan and ruhun, and the singular of ruhun

x: God Almighty says: And We made for their houses doors of silver, and couches of silver.

c: As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: and Sarar said: Silver beds.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement: And for their houses are doors and couches upon which they recline, he said: The doors are of silver, and the couches are of silver upon which they recline, he says: They recline upon the couches.

x: And his saying: And decorations means: And we would have made for them decorations in addition to that, which is gold. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: and decorations, which is gold.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: And adornments, he said: gold. Al-Hasan said: A house of adornments, he said: gold.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And ornaments. Ornamentation means gold. He said: By God, she disliked clothes of ostentation. And he mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Beware of red, for it is one of the most beloved adornments to Satan.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And decorations, he said: gold.

c: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And decorations, he said: gold.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And decorations, “We made this for the people of disbelief,” meaning for their houses, a roof of silver and what was mentioned with it. He said: And decoration is what is called the roof, and the stairways, doors, and beds of furniture, furnishings, and furnishings.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And ornaments, meaning gold. And ornaments, according to this statement of Ibn Zayd, are what people make in their homes of furnishings, furnishings, and tools. There are two interpretations of the accusative of al-Zukhruf 43:One of them is that its meaning is: For We have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious, roofs of silver and ornaments for their homes. Since the verb to climb was not repeated, and the meaning is the same, it is as if it was said: And ornaments He makes that for them from it. The second interpretation is that it is conjoined with the thrones, so its meaning is: For We have made for them these things of silver, and We have made for them gold along with that, to be rich for them with which they will be content. If the revelation had come with a genitive of az-Zukhruf, it would have been: For We have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Gracious, roofs of silver and ornaments for their homes, so ornaments would have been conjoined with silver. As for the word ma’arij, its plural is mafa’il, and its singular is mi’raj, according to the plural of mi’raj, just as the word miftah is pluralized as mafātih, according to the plural of miftah, because they are two languages: mi’raj and miftah. If the word ma’arij was pluralized as mafātih, it would have been correct, just as the word miftah is pluralized as mifātih, since its singular is mi’raj. And His statement:
h
And all of that is but the enjoyment of worldly life

, meaning that the Most High says: All of these things that you mentioned, such as the ceiling made of silver, the stairways, the doors, the beds made of silver, and the decorations, are nothing but enjoyment that the people of this world enjoy in this world. And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous, meaning that the Most High says: And the adornment of the Hereafter and its splendor are with your Lord for the righteous, meaning that those who feared God and feared His punishment, and were diligent in obeying Him, and were wary of disobeying Him specifically, to the exclusion of others among God’s creation.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous, in particular.

x: God the Most High says: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of God and does not fear His power, nor dread His punishment - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. He says: We appoint for him a devil to mislead him, and he is to him a companion.

He is to Satan a companion, that he becomes like that. The root of ‘asha is to look without certainty due to an ailment in the eye. It is said from this: So-and-so became blind, ya’sha ‘ashawan and ‘ashawan: if his sight weakens and his eye becomes dark, as if a film is over it, as the poet said: When you come to him and spend the night by the light of his fire, you will find plenty of firewood and a blazing fire.

Meaning: When you are in need, his wife will help you. But if he loses his sight and cannot see, then it is said about him: So-and-so has gone dark, he has gone dark, a deficient dark. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: She saw a man who was absent from the visitors, of different appearance, blind and blind. It is said of him: a blind man and a blind woman. The meaning of the statement is: And whoever does not look at God’s proofs by turning away from them except with a weak look, like the look of someone whose sight has been blinded, We will make him a devil. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil
means: If he turns away from the remembrance of God, We appoint for him a devil who is to him a companion.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful
, he said: He turns away.

x: Some of them interpreted it to mean: and whoever interprets it as such, then it must be read as <and whoever lives>with a fat-ha on the shin, as I explained before.
Mention of those who interpreted it thus:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement:
h
And whoever is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful
, he said: Whoever is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful.

evidence.text: Some of them interpreted it to mean: and whoever interprets it as such, then it must be read as <and whoever lives>with a fat-ha on the shin, as I explained before.

x: And His statement: And indeed, they avert them from the path, God the Exalted says: And indeed, the devils avert those who are blind to the remembrance of God, from the path of truth, so they make misguidance seem attractive to them, and make faith in God and working in obedience to Him hateful to them. And they think that they are guided, He says: And the polytheists think that, because the devils make their misguidance seem attractive to them, they are on the truth and the right path. God the Exalted informs us about them that they are on the path of polytheism out of doubt and without insight. And God the Exalted says: And indeed, they avert them from the path, so He mentioned them in the same way as mentioning all, but He mentioned one before, so He said: The opposite of him is a devil, because even though the word devil is one, it has the meaning of a plural.

The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: until he comes to us. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, except for Ibn Muhaysin, some of the Kufians and some of the Sham reciters read it as <until he comes to us>in the dual form, meaning: until this one who was blind to the remembrance of the Most Gracious comes to us, and his companion whom was appointed for him from among the devils. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra and Ibn Muhaysin read it as: until he comes to us in the singular form, meaning: until this one of the sons of Adam who was blind to the remembrance of the Most Gracious comes to us. The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is that they are two readings with similar meanings, because in the report of God, the Blessed and Exalted, about the state of one of the two groups when he arrives at it, as we have acknowledged in this world, there is enough for the listener to know the report of the other, since the report of the state of one of them is known by the report of the state of the other.

And despite that, they are two readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions, so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until he and his companion came to us together. And His saying: Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts. God Almighty says: One of these two companions said to his other companion: I would that between me and you was the distance of the two easts: meaning the distance of the east and the west, so the name of one of them prevailed over the other, as it was said: like the two moons, and as the poet said: We have taken the horizons of the sky upon you, for us are its two moons and the rising stars. As the other said: Basra and Azd are ours, Iraq is ours, Mosul and Egypt are ours, and the Holy Mosque is ours. Meaning: Mosul and Al-Jazira, so he said: The two Mosuls, and Mosul prevailed. It has been said that what he meant by his saying:
h
After the two easts is the east of winter and the east of summer

. This is because the sun rises in the winter from one east and in the summer from another east. Likewise, the west sets in two different wests, as God Almighty said: Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests (al-Rahman 55:17). He mentioned that this is what one of them said to his companion when each of them was sticking to his companion until he led him to Hell.

x: Those who said that: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said:

c: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Sa’id al-Jariri, he said:
m: It has reached me that when the unbeliever is raised from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, Satan will strike him with his hand and will not leave him until God sends them both to the Fire. That is when he will say: Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! What an evil companion! As for the believer, an angel will be assigned to him and he will be with him until he says: Either he will judge between the people, or we will be taken to whatever God wills.
