And despite that, they are two readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions, so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct.

x: And His statement: And it will not benefit you today O you who live without remembering God in this world when you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment means: Your sharing in it will not be lightened for you today from God’s punishment, because each one of you has his share of it, and that in His statement: that you is in the nominative case because I mentioned that its meaning is: Your sharing will not benefit you.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Can you then make the deaf hear? He whom God has deprived of hearing His arguments which He has presented in this Book, thus making him deaf to them, or can you guide to the path of guidance he whose heart God has blinded from his sight, and over whom Satan has taken control, making destruction seem attractive to him? And he who is in manifest error? He says: Or can you guide he who has strayed from the straight path, following a path other than the truth, his error clearly showing that he is straying from the truth and deviating from the straight path. God the Almighty says: That is not up to you, rather that is up to God, in whose hand is the turning of the hearts of His creation as He wills. You are only a warner, so convey the warning to them.
And His statement:
h
If We take you away
, We will surely take retribution from them.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meanings of this threat.
Some of them said: It refers to the people of Islam from the nation of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: But
h
if We take you away

, We will surely take retribution from them. He said: There was a severe punishment after the Prophet of God, so God, the Most High, honored His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by showing him in his nation what punishment there was after him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
But if We should take you away, We will surely take retribution from them.

So God took away His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and did not see in his nation anything except that which would please his eyes, and God left the punishment after him, and there is no prophet who did not see punishment in his nation, or who did not say what he desired. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was shown what his nation would encounter after him, and he remained contracted and did not relax and laugh until he met God, the Blessed and Exalted.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said:
m: Qatada recited: But if We should take you away - indeed, We will take retribution from them. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has gone, but the retribution remains. God did not see anything that His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) disliked in his nation until he passed away. There was never a prophet who did not see punishment in his nation, except your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was shown what would befall his nation after him, and he was never seen smiling or cheerful until God took him.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the polytheists of Quraysh, and they said: God has shown His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, among them.
Those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then whether We take you away, We will take retribution from them
as We took retribution from previous nations,
h
or We show you that which We promised them

, God showed him that and made it manifest to him. This second statement is the more correct of the two interpretations, because it is in the context of God’s statement about the polytheists, so it is more appropriate for it to be a threat to them than a warning to one who was not mentioned. So the meaning of the statement, since that is the case, is: If We take you away, O Muhammad, from among these polytheists and extract you from them, We will take retribution from them, as We did that with other nations that rejected their messengers, or We show you that which We promised them, O Muhammad, of victory over them and your supremacy over them, We are powerful over them, that We will make you victorious over them and disgrace them by your hand and the hands of those who believe in you.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So, O Muhammad, hold fast to what this Qur’an that your Lord revealed to you commands you to do. Indeed, you are on a straight path and a sound method. That is the religion of God that He commanded, which is Islam.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: “
h
So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you
. Indeed, you are on a straight path”: meaning Islam.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are on a straight path.”

x: And His statement: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, God Almighty says: And indeed, this Qur’an that was revealed to you, O Muhammad, which We have commanded you to hold fast to, is an honor for you and your people from Quraysh. And you will be asked, He says: And your Lord will ask you and them about what you did in it, and whether you did what your Lord commanded you in it, and refrained from what He forbade you in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, he said: He says to the man: Who are you? He says: From the Arabs. It is said: From which Arabs? He says: From Quraysh.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and it is this Qur’an.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people. He said: An honor for you and your people, meaning the Qur’an.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, he said: Was not the prophecy and the Qur’an that was revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a reminder for him and his people?

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement:
h
And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers
, and who were the ones whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to ask that.

Some of them said that the ones whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to ask that were the believers among the People of the Two Books: the Torah and the Gospel.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abd al-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: In the recitation of Abdullah bin Masoud: And ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers
. This is the reading of Abdullah: Ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers

, meaning: Ask the people of the Torah and the Gospel: Did the messengers come to them except with the message of monotheism, that they should worship God alone? He said: And in some readings: And ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you, “Did We appoint other gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?”

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding some of the letters of the verse, And ask those to whom We sent before you of Our messengers. Ask the People of the Book: Did the messengers not bring them monotheism? Did they not bring them sincerity?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement:
h
And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers
, in the reading of Ibn Masʿud: Ask those who read the Scripture before you, meaning: the believers among the People of the Scripture.

x: Others said: Rather, those who were ordered to be questioned were the prophets who gathered for him on the night of his ascension to the Holy House.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And ask those We sent before you… the verse

, he said: They gathered for him on the night of his Night Journey to Jerusalem, so he led them in prayer and God said to him: Ask them. He said: So he had stronger faith and certainty in God and in what came to him from God than to ask them, and he recited: And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who read the Scripture before you
r
(Yunus 10:94)

. He said: So he was not in doubt, and he did not ask the prophets, nor those who read the Scripture. He said: And Gabriel, peace be upon him, called, and I said to myself: Now our father Abraham will lead us in faith. He said: So Gabriel pushed me on my back and said: Come forward, O Muhammad, and pray, and he recited: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram (al-Isra’ 17:1)… until he reached: To show him some of Our signs (al-Isra’ 17:1). The more correct of the two interpretations of this is the one that says: What he meant by it is: Ask the believers of the People of the Two Books.

x: How can it be said, Ask the Messengers, meaning, Ask the believers in them and their Books?

This is permissible because the believers in them and their Books are the ones who convey from them what they brought to them from their Lord. So, reporting about them and what they brought from their Lord, if authentic, means reporting them, and asking about what they brought means asking them if the one being asked is knowledgeable about them and truthful about them.

This is similar to God’s command to us to refer our disputes to God and to the Messenger, when He says: And if you disagree about anything, refer it to God and the Messenger 4:59. It is known that the meaning of this is: refer it to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, because referring to that is referring to God and the Messenger. Similarly, His statement,
h
And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers

, means: ask the books of those We sent before you of the messengers, for you know the authenticity of that from before us. So, mentioning the Messengers is sufficient instead of mentioning the Books, since its meaning is known. And His statement:
h
Did We make gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful

? He says: Did We command them to worship gods besides God in what they brought them, or did they come to believe that we commanded them to do so? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
h
And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers
: Did We ever appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?
Those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Have We made other than the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped? Did the messengers come to them commanding them to worship gods other than God? It was also said: gods to be worshipped, so he brought out the report about the gods in the same way as he brought out the report about the males of the children of Adam, and he did not say: are worshipped, nor are they worshipped, so it is made feminine and they are stones or some inanimate objects as is done in the report about some inanimate objects. He did that in this way, because they were worshipped and venerated as people venerate their kings and leaders, so he brought out the report about them in the same way as he brought out the report about the kings and nobles of the children of Adam.

evidence.text: Abd al-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: In the recitation of Abdullah bin Masoud: And ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you.
This is the reading of Abdullah: Ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you.

It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers, in the reading of Ibn Masʿud: Ask those who read the Scripture before you, meaning: the believers among the People of the Scripture.

x: God Almighty says: And We sent, O Muhammad, Moses with Our proofs to Pharaoh and the nobles of his people, just as We sent you to these polytheists from your people. Moses said to them: I am the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, just as you said to your people from Quraysh 106:I am the Messenger of God to you.

So when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them. He says: So when Moses came to Pharaoh and his people with Our arguments and proofs of the truth of what he was saying, in what he called them to of the Oneness of God and disavowal of the worship of deities, at once Pharaoh and his people laughed at the signs and lessons that Moses brought them, just as your people mock the signs and lessons that you brought them. This is a consolation from God the Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he was experiencing at the hands of the polytheists of his people, and an announcement from Him to him that his people of polytheism would not go beyond being like the rest of the nations who followed their path of disbelief in God and denial of His Messengers. And He urged His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to follow the example of the resolute Messengers in being patient with them, and He informed him that the consequence of their return to ruin and destruction would be like His example with those who rebelled against Him before them, and His victory over them and His exaltation of His command, just as He did with Moses, peace be upon him, and his people who believed in him, by giving them victory over Pharaoh and his people.

God Almighty says: And We did not show Pharaoh and his chiefs any sign, meaning: Our proof against him of the truth of what our Messenger Moses was calling him to do, “except that it was greater than its sister, meaning: “Except that which We showed him of that was greater in proof against them and more emphatic than the signs that came before it, and more indicative of the truth of what Moses was commanding him to do of the Oneness of God.” His statement:
h
And We seized them with punishment
means: We brought down punishment upon them, and that is like the Almighty’s seizing them with years of drought, a decrease in fruits, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood. His statement:
h
Perhaps they will return
means: So that they may return from their disbelief in God to His Oneness and obedience, and repentance from the sins they are committing.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We seized them with punishment that perhaps they would return
, meaning that they would repent or remember.

x: God Almighty says: Pharaoh and his nobles said to Moses: O magician, call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you. What they meant by their saying: according to what He has promised you is His promise that He made to you: If we believe in you and follow you, He will remove the punishment from us.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, regarding the statement of God Almighty: By what He has promised you, he said: If we believe, the punishment will be removed from us.

q.l: If someone were to ask us:
x: What is the point of their saying, O magician, call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you, and how could they call him a magician when they were asking him to call upon his Lord to remove the punishment from them?
To them, magician meant scholar, and magic was not considered reprehensible to them. They only called him by this name because its meaning to them was O knowledgeable one.

And His saying: Indeed, we are guided, means: They said: We are your followers, so we believe in what you have brought us, and we believe in the Oneness of God, so we see the path of righteousness. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: “O magician, call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you. Indeed, we are guided.” He said: They said, O Moses: Call upon your Lord for us. If you remove this punishment from us, we will believe in you.

x: And His statement: So when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their covenant. God Almighty says: So when We removed from them the punishment which We had sent down upon them, which they had promised that if it were removed from them they would be guided to the path of truth, at once after We removed that from them they broke the covenant which they had made with Us. He says: They betrayed and persisted in their misguidance, and persisted in their error. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: If they break their oath: meaning they betray.

x: God Almighty says: And Pharaoh called out to his people from the Copts, and said, ‘O my people, is not mine the kingdom of Egypt, and these rivers flowing beneath me?
h
Do you not see
?’ What he means by his saying: beneath me is: from before me in Paradise.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And these rivers flow beneath me, he said: They had gardens and rivers of water. And His statement:
h
Do you not see
? He is saying:
h
Do you not see

, O people, what I am in of bliss and goodness, and what Moses is in of poverty and speechlessness? He boasted about his rule over Egypt, the enemy of God, and the worldly life that God had given him as a lure from Him. He thought that what he was in of that he had attained by his own hand and power, and that Moses had not attained what he was describing. Therefore, he attributed it to humiliation, arguing against the ignorant of his people that if Moses, peace be upon him, had been truthful in what he brought of signs and lessons, and that it had not been magic, he would have gained for himself of kingship and bliss, like what he was in of that, out of ignorance of God and deceit from him by His dictation to him.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what Pharaoh said to his people after he argued with them about his kingdom and authority, and the clarity of his tongue and the perfection of his creation, and the difference between him and Moses with the attributes with which he described himself and Moses: I am better, O people, and my description is this description that I have described to you,
h
Or am I better than this one who is humiliated

? He has nothing of the kingdom and wealth with the illness in his body, and the affliction in his tongue, because of which he can hardly articulate his speech? There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of his saying: Or in this place.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: Rather, I am better. They said: That is a statement, not a question.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his statement:
h
Or am I better than this one who is humiliated
? He said: Rather, I am better than this. The people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the Arabic language used to say something similar.

x: Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is from the interrogative which was made with am because it is connected to a statement before it. He said: If you wish, you can return it to his saying: Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine? If the statement is directed to it being an interrogative, then there must be something omitted in the statement, and it is sufficient to mention what was mentioned from what was left out, and the meaning of the statement then is: Am I better, O people, than this one who is humiliated, or is he? It was mentioned about some readers that he used to read: Am I not better?
Al-Farra' narrated this to me, saying:

c: One of the elders told me that
m: he had heard that some of the reciters read in this way. If this reading had been widespread among the reciters of the regions, it would have been correct and its meaning would have been good. However, it is contrary to what the reciters of the regions do, so I do not permit it to be read in this way. And based on this reading, if it were correct, there would be no difficulty or effort in understanding its meaning. The correct reading in this regard is what the reciters of the regions have followed. The most appropriate interpretation of the statement, since this is the case, is the interpretation of those who made or am I better? from the question that was made with am, because of its connection to what preceded it in the statement, and directed it to mean: Am I better than this one who is humiliated, or is he? Then he left out mentioning am he, because of the evidence in the statement for that. And what he meant by his saying: Who is this one who is humiliated? is: Who is this one who is weak due to his little wealth, and that he does not have the kingship and authority that he has. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Or am I better than this one who is humiliated
? He said: Weak.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Who is this who is humiliated? He said: The humiliated is the weak. His saying:
h
And he can hardly articulate it
means: He can hardly articulate the words due to his tongue’s defect. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: and he can hardly make himself clear: meaning he has a weak tongue.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And he can hardly make clear the speech.

evidence.text: It was mentioned about some readers that he used to read: Am I not better?
One of the elders told me that he had heard that some of the reciters read in this way.
If this reading had been widespread among the reciters of the regions, it would have been correct and its meaning would have been good.
However, it is contrary to what the reciters of the regions do, so I do not permit it to be read in this way.
And based on this reading, if it were correct, there would be no difficulty or effort in understanding its meaning.
The correct reading in this regard is what the reciters of the regions have followed.

x: And his statement:
h
Why were not bracelets of gold bestowed upon him
? means: Why was not
h
a bracelet of gold

bestowed upon Moses, if he was truthful that he was the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds? It is the plural of bracelet, which is the heart that is placed on the hand. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
A bracelet of gold
means: A necklace of gold.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
A bracelet of gold

means a necklace of gold. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Basra, and Kufa recited it as Why were bracelets of gold not bestowed upon him? It was mentioned that Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to recite it as bracelets of gold. The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is what the countries read, even though the other has a correct meaning. Arabic: Some grammarians of Basra said: Usawrah is the plural of Iswar. He said: Asawrah is the plural of Aswar. He said: Whoever reads it as Asawura means Asawir, and God knows best, so he replaced the Ya, like Zanadiqa, in which the Ha replaced the Ya in Zanadiq. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Whoever reads Asawura makes its singular Iswar, and whoever reads Usawrah makes its singular Suwar. He said: Asawrah may be the plural of Usawrah, just as the plural of Asqi is Asqi, and the plural of Akra’ is Akare’. Another of them said: It has been said about the bracelet of the hand: Aswar and Aswar are permissible for it. He said: According to this language, Asawrah may be its plural.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’
m: that he used to say: The singular of bracelets is iswar. He said: And his confirmation in the reading of Abu ibn Ka’b is:
h
Why were not bracelets of gold bestowed upon him

? If what was narrated in the narration is true, that it is permissible to say about the bracelet of the hand is iswar, then there is no difficulty in the plural of asawwara, and I do not know of that being correct from the Arabs with any narration from them, because what is known in their speech of the meaning of iswar is: the archer, the skilled archer from the Persian men. As for that which is worn on the hand, what is known from its name among them is bracelet. If that is the case, then what is more appropriate for asawwara is that it is the plural of aswara, according to what was said by the one whose opinion we have mentioned in that regard. And his saying:
h
Or the angels came with him in pairs

, meaning: Or if he was truthful, why did the angels not come with him in pairs, some of them paired with others, so that they would follow one another and testify to him that he is a messenger of God to them? In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, with differences among them in the expression of its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: They walk together.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
The angels are paired
, he said: They walk together.

x: Others said: consecutive.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Or the angels came with him in pairs
: meaning in succession.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

x: Others said: They compare each other.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
Or the angels came with him in pairs
. He said: They were paired with each other.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Medina, Basra, and Kufa recited it as Why were bracelets of gold not bestowed upon him?
It was mentioned that Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to recite it as bracelets of gold.
He said: Whoever reads it as Asawura means Asawir, and God knows best, so he replaced the Ya, like Zanadiqa, in which the Ha replaced the Ya in Zanadiq.
He said: And his confirmation in the reading of Abu ibn Ka’b is: Why were not bracelets of gold bestowed upon him?

x: God the Almighty says: So Pharaoh made light of some of his people from among the Copts, by saying what God the Blessed and Exalted informed us that he said to them, so they accepted it from him and obeyed him, and denied Moses. God the Almighty said: They only obeyed and responded to what the enemy of God called them to, to believe in him and deny Moses, because they were a people who had turned away from the obedience of God, due to His abandonment of them and His seal upon their hearts.
God Almighty says:
h
So when they angered Us
, meaning by His saying they angered Us: they made Us angry. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
So when they angered us
means: they angered us.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: When they angered us, he said: When they angered us.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
So when they angered us
: they made us angry.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
So when they angered Us
, he said: They angered their Lord.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: When they angered us, he said: They made us angry.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: So when they grieved us, he said: they angered us, and it is like the words of Jacob: Oh, my grief for Joseph
r
(Yusuf 12:84)
, he said: Oh, my sorrow for Joseph.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
So when they angered Us
h
We took retribution from them
, he said: They angered Us. And His statement:
h
We took retribution from them
means:
h
We took retribution from them
with the immediate punishment that We hastened for them, so We drowned them all in the sea.

x: The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except for Asim, recited it <‫صففان‬ ‫>فجالعناهم‬with a damma on the seen and the lam, referring that to the plural of salif from the people, who is the one who is in front of the people. Al-Farra’ narrated that he heard Al-Qasim bin Ma’n mention that he heard the Arabs say: A salif from the people has passed away. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and Asim, recited it: ‫صففان‬ ‫فجالعناهم‬ with a fatha on the seen and the lam. When it is recited in this way, it is possible that it refers to a group, an individual, a male or a female, because it is said to al-Nas 114:You are our salaf, and it can also be plural, so it is said: They are asfal. From this is the report narrated from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said: The righteous go as salaf. Humayd Al-A’raj used to recite it: < ‫فجالعناهم‬ ‫>صففان‬with a damma on the seen and a fatha on the lam, referring that to the plural of salif from the people, like ummah minhum nation and qata’a a group.

The most correct reading of this is the one that opens the seen and the lam, because it is the pure language and the well-known speech of the Arabs, and the most deserving of the languages to read the Book of God from the languages of the Arabs, the most eloquent and famous of them. So the interpretation of the statement is: So We made those whom We drowned from the people of Pharaoh in the sea an advance to the Fire, the disbelievers of your people, O Muhammad, from Quraysh, and the disbelievers of your people are behind them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said:

c: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
So We made them a precedent and an example for later generations
, he said: The unbelievers of the people of Pharaoh were a precedent for the unbelievers of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So We made them predecessors in the Fire.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar:
m: So We made them predecessors. He said: predecessors to the Fire. His statement:
h
And an example for others

means: And a lesson and an admonition from which the nations who came after them would learn a lesson, so that they would stop disbelieving in God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And an example for others
, he said: A lesson for those who come after them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And an example for others
: meaning a lesson for others.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And an example for others
: meaning a lesson for those who come after them.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: So We made them a precedent and an example. He said: A lesson. And His statement:
h
And when the son of Mary was cited as an example

, God Almighty says: And when God likened Jesus in His creation and formation of him without a male relative to Adam, He likened him to him in that He created him from dust without a male relative, then your people, O Muhammad, are making a fuss about that and saying: Muhammad wants nothing from us except that we take him as a god whom we worship, just as the Christians worshipped Christ.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: When your people turn away from him, he said: They make a noise. He said: Quraysh said: Muhammad only wants us to worship him as the people of Jesus worshipped Jesus.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: When Jesus, son of Mary, was mentioned, the Quraysh were alarmed by that and said: O Muhammad, why did you mention Jesus, son of Mary? They said:

The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except for Asim, recited it <‫صففان‬ ‫>فجالعناهم‬with a damma on the seen and the lam, referring that to the plural of salif from the people, who is the one who is in front of the people.

When it is recited in this way, it is possible that it refers to a group, an individual, a male or a female, because it is said to al-Nas 114:You are our salaf, and it can also be plural, so it is said: They are asfal.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will surely enter it. (al-Anbiya 21:89) The polytheists were told when it was revealed: We are satisfied that our gods be with Jesus, Ezra, and the angels, because all of these are among those who are worshipped besides God. God Almighty said: And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, at once your people turned away from him. And they said: Are our gods better, or is he?
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, at once your people turn away from it. He said: He meant the Quraysh when it was said to them: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be brought to it. (al-Anbiya 21:89) So the Quraysh said to him: And who is the son of Mary? He said: He is the servant of God and His Messenger. h

, he said: The Jews and the Christians. This is a straight path.” And His statement:
h
So woe to those who have wronged from the punishment of a painful Day

. h
Do they await anything but the Hour

, that it should come upon them suddenly? He says: Do these disputing parties regarding Jesus, son of Mary, who say falsehood about him, await anything but the Hour in which the Resurrection will come suddenly? And they perceive not. He says: And they do not know of its coming.

God Almighty says: Those who were friends on the Day of Resurrection for committing sins against God in this world will be enemies to one another, disowning one another, except for those who were friends for fear of God. , except for the righteous, so every friend who commits a sin against God in this world will be enemies to one another.
