m: regarding his statement:
h
Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another
, except for the righteous. So every friendship is enmity except the friendship of the righteous.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq,
m: that Ali may God be pleased with him said: Two friends are believers and two friends are unbelievers. Then one of the believers died and he said: O Lord, so-and-so used to command me to obey You and obey Your Messenger, and he used to command me to do good and forbid me from evil, and he used to tell me that I would meet You. O Lord, do not lead him astray after me, and guide him as You have guided me, and honor him as You have honored me. Then when his believing friend died, He would bring them together and say: Let one of you praise the other, and say: O Lord, he used to command me to obey You and obey Your Messenger, and he used to command me to do good, and forbid me from evil, and he used to tell me that I would meet You. Then He would say: What a good friend, what a good brother, and what a good companion! He said: One of the unbelievers dies and says: O Lord, so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and obeying Your Messenger, and he used to command me to do evil, and he used to forbid me from doing good, and he used to tell me that I would not meet You. So He said: What a bad brother, what a bad friend, and what a bad companion!

x: And His statement:
h
O My servants

, there is no fear concerning you today, nor shall you grieve. In these statements there is an omission that is sufficient due to the evidence of what was mentioned. The meaning of the statement is: Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous, for it will be said to them:
h
O My servants

, there is no fear concerning you today from My punishment, for I have made you safe from it through My pleasure with you, nor shall you grieve over parting from this world, for what you have come to is better for you than what you parted from it. He mentioned that people will be called out with this call on the Day of Resurrection, and those who are not among its people will covet it until they hear the words: Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims, and then they will despair of it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I heard that when the people are resurrected, there will be none among them who will not be terrified. Then a caller will call out: O servants of God, there is no fear concerning you today, nor will you grieve. Then all the people will hope for it. He said: Then it will be followed by those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims. He said: Then the people, except the Muslims, will despair of it.

x: And His statement:
h
Those who believed in Our verses

, God Almighty says: O My servants who believed, and they are those who believed in the Book of God and His Messengers, and did what their Messengers brought them, and were Muslims, meaning: and they were people of submission to God in their hearts, and accepted what their Messengers brought them from their Lord, according to the religion of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, may God bless him and grant him peace, upright, neither Jews nor Christians, nor people of idols.

And His saying: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing. God Almighty says: Enter Paradise, you believers, and your spouses, blessed by God’s honor, happy with what your Lord has given you today.

The people of interpretation have differed in their interpretation of His statement: You will be informed. We have mentioned what has been said about this previously, and we have explained the correct opinion regarding it in our view, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. However, we will mention some of the opinions of the people of interpretation that were not mentioned there.
Mention of who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, in happiness: meaning, you will be in comfort.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: You will be delighted, he said: You will be in bliss.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: You are honoured, he said: You are respected.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: You and your wives will be happy, he said: You will be in comfort.

x: God Almighty says: Those who believed in His verses in this world, when they enter Paradise in the Hereafter, will be served with golden plates. This is the plural of plate. A plate is a bowl. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of who said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: They will be served with golden plates, he said: Bowls.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said:
m: “The lowest-ranking person in Paradise is he who has a palace in which there are seventy thousand servants, in the hand of each servant is a plate in addition to what is in the hand of its owner. If his door were opened and the people of this world were to host him, he would be more spacious than them.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, who said:
m: “The lowest-ranking person in Paradise is he who has seventy thousand servants, with each servant a golden plate. If all the people of the Earth were to descend upon him, it would be spacious for them. He will not seek help from anyone else. This is in the words of God Almighty: ‘They will have therein whatever they wish, and with Us is more.’”
r
and They will have therein whatever their souls desire and their eyes delight in.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said:
m: There is no one from the people of Paradise except that a thousand young men strive for him, each young man doing the same work as his companion. His saying:
h
And cups is the plural of cup

, and the cup is the round-headed pitcher, which has no ear or spout, and it is what Al-A’sha meant when he said: A delicious, creamy dish with a hint of butter between its cup and ear And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And cups He said: The cups that have no spouts. The meaning of the statement is: Food will be served to them there in golden plates, and drink in golden cups. So the mention of the plates and cups was dispensed with in place of the mention of the food and drink that will be therein so that the listeners will know its meaning. <And therein is whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in>God the Almighty says: For you in Paradise, O believers, is whatever your souls desire and your eyes delight in. And you will abide therein eternally He says: And you will remain therein, never to leave it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Ibn Sabit,
m: “A man said: O Messenger of God, I love horses. Are there horses in Paradise? He said: If He wills, He will admit you to Paradise. You will not wish to ride a horse of red rubies that will fly with you wherever you wish in Paradise except that you will do so. A Bedouin said: O Messenger of God, I love camels. Are there camels in Paradise? He said: O Bedouin, if God wills, He will admit you to Paradise, and in it there is whatever your soul desires and your eyes delight in.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa narrated to us, saying: Umar bin Abdul Rahman Al-Abbar narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Saad Al-Ansari, on the authority of Abu Dhabia Al-Salfi, who said:
m: “A group of the people of Paradise will be shaded by a cloud, and it will say: ‘What rain has it given you?’ He said: ‘No one among the people will supplicate for something except that it will rain on them, until one of them will say: ‘We will be given rain from young maidens of our age.’”

c: Ibn Arafa told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Al-Walid, who said:
m: Mujahid was asked, Is there hearing in Paradise? He said, There is a tree in it called Al-Ays, which has a hearing like no other that has been heard.

c: Musa bin Abd al-Rahman told me: Zaid bin Habbab told us: Muawiyah bin Salih told us: Sulayman bin Amir told us:
m: I heard Abu Umamah say: A man from the people of Paradise will desire a bird while it is flying, and it will fall fully cooked in his hand, and he will eat from it until he is done, then he will fly away. And he will desire a drink, and the pitcher will fall into his hand, and he will drink from it as much as he wants, then he will return to his place. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: And in it is whatever the souls desire. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Syria read it as what they desire with an additional ha’, and this is also the case in their copies of the Qur’an. The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it as desires without a ha’, and this is also the case in their copies of the Qur’an. There will be passed around them trays of gold and goblets, and therein will be whatever the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement: And in it is whatever the souls desire.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Syria read it as what they desire with an additional ha’, and this is also the case in their copies of the Qur’an.
The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it as desires without a ha’, and this is also the case in their copies of the Qur’an.

x: God Almighty says: It will be said to them: This is Paradise which God has made you inherit from the people of Hell whom He has put into Hell because of the good deeds you did in this world.
For you therein means: For you in Paradise there is much fruit of every kind. From it you will eat means: From the fruit you will eat whatever you desire.

God Almighty says: Indeed, the criminals - those who committed disbelief in God in this world, and will commit it in the Hereafter - will abide in the punishment of Hell eternally. He says: They will remain in it, and it will not be lightened for them. He says: The punishment will not be lightened for them. The root of weakness is weakness.
h
And they are therein in despair
He says: And they are in the torment of Hell in despair, and the ha in fih is from the mention of the torment. It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah it is: <
h
And they are therein in despair

>and the meaning is: And they are in Hell in despair, and the one who is in despair in this place is: the one who has despaired of salvation and has given in to the torment and affliction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: and they are in despair therein: meaning they are resigned.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they are therein in despair
, he said: hopeless.

x: Others said: Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: and they are in despair therein means their condition has changed. We have previously explained the meaning of Iblas with evidence, and mentioned those who differed about it, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

evidence.text: It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah it is: <And they are therein in despair>and the meaning is: And they are in Hell in despair, and the one who is in despair in this place is: the one who has despaired of salvation and has given in to the torment and affliction.

x: And His statement: And We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers. God Almighty says: We did not wrong these criminals by what We told you, O people, that We did to them of the torment of Hell. But it was they who were the wrongdoers, by worshipping in this world someone other than the One they were supposed to worship, and by disbelieving in God and denying His Oneness.

God Almighty says: And these criminals, after God had put them into Hell and they had been afflicted therein with the affliction that befell them, called out to Malik, the keeper of Hell: O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us. He said: Let your Lord kill us and finish killing us. It was mentioned that Malik would not answer them at the time they said that to him, and would leave them for a thousand years after that, then he would answer them and say to them: You will remain.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And they will call out
, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us,’ so he answered them after a thousand years, Indeed, you will remain.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of a man from among his neighbors called al-Hasan, on the authority of Nawf,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And they will cry out
, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!’ He said: He will leave them for one hundred years of your count, then He will call out to them and say: O people of the Fire, you will remain.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said:
m: h
And they will cry out

, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!’ He said: So He left them alone for forty years without answering them, then He answered them: Indeed, you will remain. “Our Lord, bring us out of it, but if we return, we will be wrongdoers.” (al-Mu’minun 23:107) So He left them alone for the duration of the world, then He answered them: Be gone into it, despised and disgraced, and do not speak to me. (al-Mu’minun 23:108) He said: “By God, the people did not utter a word after the word. There was nothing but sighs and inhalations.”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Azdi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said:
m: The people of Hell call upon Malik for forty years, but he does not answer them. Then he says: You will remain. Then they call upon their Lord: Our Lord, take us out of it, for if we return, then we will be wrongdoers. He leaves them or leaves them alone for as long as the world. Then he says to them: Get out into it, disgraced and do not speak to me. He said: After that, the people did not utter a word, except for sighing and sobbing in the fire of Hell.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Nawf,
m: h
And they will call out
, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us.’ He said: He will leave them for one hundred years of your count. Then he called out to them and they responded to him, and he said: You will remain.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And they will call out

, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!’ He said: Malik is the keeper of Hellfire. He said: So they remained for a thousand years of your reckoning. He said: Then He answered them after a thousand years: You will remain.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
And they will cry out
, ‘O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us,’ he said: Let us die. The decree here is death. So He answered them, Indeed, you will remain.

x: And his saying:
h
We have certainly come to you with the truth
means: We have sent to you, O people of Quraysh, our Messenger Muhammad with the truth.

c: As Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Indeed, We have brought you the truth, he said: What Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. But most of you are averse to the truth, God Almighty says: But most of you are averse to what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought of the truth.

x: God Almighty says: Or have these polytheists from Quraysh decided on a plan and made it a reality, plotting against the truth that We have brought them? Then We will surely bring about for them that which will disgrace them and humiliate them with punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Or have they plotted a matter? Then We are plotting. He said: We are planning: If they plotted an evil, We plotted the like of it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Or have they decided upon a matter
, then We are also deciding upon it? He said:
h
Or have they decided upon a matter
, then We are also deciding upon it.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Or have they decided upon a matter
, then We are to decide upon it, he said:
h
Or have they decided upon a matter
, then We are to decide upon Our matter.

x: And His statement:
h
Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations

? He says: Or do these polytheists think that We do not hear what they have hidden from the people of their speech, and what they have consulted among themselves and whispered about it to the exclusion of others, so that We do not punish them for it because it is hidden from Us? And His statement: Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing down. God Almighty says: Rather, We know what they whisper among themselves and what they conceal from the people of their secret speech, and Our guardians are with them, meaning they are with them, writing down what they uttered of speech and spoke of their words. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about three people who argued about whether God Almighty should listen to the words of His servants.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Amr bin Saeed bin Yasar Al-Qurashi told me, he said: Abu Qutaybah told us, he said: Asim bin Muhammad Al-Amri told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, he said:
m: While three people were between the Kaaba and its curtains, two of them from Quraysh and one from Thaqafi, or two from Thaqafi and one from Quraysh, one of the three said: Do you think that God hears our speech? The first said: If we speak out loud, He hears, but if we speak in secret, He does not hear. The second said: If He hears when you speak out loud, then He hears when you speak in secret. He said: Then this verse was revealed:
h
Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations

? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing down. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement: Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing down, the people of interpretation said.

x: Mention of who said that:

c: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing down. He said: The guardians.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Yes, and Our messengers are with them, writing down. That is, with them.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers.”

Some of them said in the meaning of that: Say, O Muhammad, if the Most Gracious had a son, as you say and claim, O polytheists, then I would be the first of the believers in God in your denial, and the one who denies what you say that He has a son.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son,” as you say, then I would be the first of the worshippers, the believers in God, so say what you will.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Then I am the first of the worshippers, he said: Say: If God had a son according to what you say, then I am the first to worship God and declare Him One and to deny you.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Say, The Most Gracious has no son, so I am the first of those who worship Him in that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers,” meaning: The Most Gracious had no son, so I would be the first of the witnesses.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is negation, and the meaning of that is denial, and the interpretation of that is: that was not and should not be.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers.” Qatada said: This is a phrase from the speech of the Arabs: If the Most Gracious had a son, meaning that this did not happen, and it should not happen.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Say, ‘If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of those who worship Him,’ he said: This is a denial that the Most Gracious had no son, God denies Himself that He has a son. Rather, the word what means: the Most Gracious had no son, the Most Gracious has no son, like His statement, And if their plot was to move mountains
r
(Ibrahim 14:46)

, it means: their plot was not to move mountains, so what God has sent down from His Book and decreed from His decree is more firmly established than mountains. And if is what if what was, the Arabs say: if it was, and what you say was not. And regarding His statement, then I am the first of those who worship Him, or whoever worships God with faith and belief that the Most Gracious has no son, on this I worship God.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us:
m: I asked Ibn Muhammad about the statement of God: If the Most Gracious had a son, he said: He did not have a son.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, saying: Amr told us, saying:
m: I asked Zayd ibn Aslam about the statement of God: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son,” he said: This is a well-known statement of the Arabs, “If it was: it was not, if this matter ever happened.” Then he said: And His statement, “
h
And if it
was: it was not.”

x: Others said: The meaning of indeed in this context is the meaning of recompense. They said: The interpretation of the statement is: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would have been the first to worship Him with that.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers.” He said: If He had a son, I would have been the first to worship Him because He had a son, but He has no son.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Say, If the Most Gracious had a son, then I am the first to reject that.

i: They directed the meaning of worshippers to those who deny and reject it, from the saying of the Arabs: So-and-so has worshipped this matter if he is disgusted by it, angry, and rejects it, so he worships a slave, as the poet said:
x: Oh, I love Umm Al-Walid, and when she saw my head, she became a worshipper As the other said: Whenever a friend wants, he can sever ties with his friend and inevitably oppress him.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi’b told me, on the authority of Abu Qusayt, on the authority of Ba’jah ibn Zayd al-Juhani,
m: that a woman from among them went to her husband, who was also a man from among them, and gave birth to a child after six months. This was mentioned to Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him, so he ordered that she be stoned. Then Ali Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers." ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him went to him and said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46:15), and He said: And his weaning is in two years
r
(Luqman 31:14)

. He said: By God, Uthman did not worship until he sent for her to return. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: Abd means he refused. The first of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, that is correct is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of in is the condition that requires the reward, according to what we mentioned from al-Suddi, and that is that in does not go beyond one of two meanings in this place: either it is the letter that is in the meaning of the condition that requires the reward, or it is in the meaning of denial. And suppose if it is directed towards denial, the speech does not have much meaning, because it becomes in the meaning of: Say, the Most Gracious has no son.
h
And if it

becomes in that meaning, the ignorant people of the polytheists of God think that he only denied with that that God Almighty had a son before some time, then created a son for him after he did not have one. Although if that was its meaning, then those whom God commanded His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: The Most Gracious has no son, so I am the first of the worshippers, would have been able to say to him, you have spoken the truth, and it is as you said. We did not claim that he always had a son, but rather we said: He did not have a son, then He created the jinn and married them, so a son came to Him from them, as God informed us about them that they used to say. And God, may He be exalted, would not have provided evidence for His Prophet. May the peace and blessings of God be upon him and upon those who deny him, with the proof they are able to attack it. Since our explanation of if to mean denial is what we mentioned, then what is most similar to the two meanings of it is the condition. Since that is the case, then it is clear that what we say is correct, that the meaning of the speech is: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who claim that the angels are daughters of God: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of you to worship Him in that. But He has no son, so I worship Him because He has no son, and it is not appropriate for Him to have one. If the speech is directed to what we have said from this aspect, it is not in the form of doubt, but rather in the form of gentleness in speech and good discourse, as God Almighty said: “Say: ‘God, and either we or you are upon guidance or in manifest error’”
r
(Saba’: 24)
. He knew that he was right, and that his opponents were clearly astray.

x: And His saying:
h
Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth

, God Almighty says: To exonerate and sanctify the Owner of the heavens and the earth and the Owner of the Throne who encompasses all of that, and what is in that of creation, which these polytheists falsely describe Him with, and which they attribute to Him of a son and other things that should not be attributed to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
The Lord of the Throne is above what they describe
: meaning what they lie about.

x: God Almighty says: So, O Muhammad, leave these slanderers against God, who describe Him as having a son, to indulge in their falsehood and play in their worldly life until they meet the Day they are promised, which is the Day when God will burn them in Hell for their slander against Him, and that is the Day of Resurrection.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: until they meet the Day they are promised, he said: The Day of Resurrection. And His statement:
h
And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth

, God Almighty says: And God, to whom belong divinity, is worshipped in the heaven and on earth, just as He is worshipped in the heaven. There is nothing worthy of worship other than Him. God Almighty says: So single out worship for the One with this description, and do not associate anything with Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth
, he said: He is worshipped in the heaven and is worshipped on the earth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth
: meaning He is worshipped in the heaven and on the earth. And His saying:
h
And He is the Wise
, the Knowing, means: He is the Wise in managing His creation and subjecting them to whatever He wills, and the Knowing of their interests.

x: God Almighty says: Blessed be He to whom belongs authority over the seven heavens and the earth, and all that is between them. His rule applies over all of that, and His decree is carried out concerning them. He says: How can He have a partner when His rule and judgment are effective over them? And with Him is knowledge of the Hour. He says: And with Him is knowledge of the Hour when the scum will rise and creation will be gathered from their graves for the place of reckoning. His statement: And to Him you will return. He says: And to Him, O people, you will return after your death, so you will go to Him and He will reward the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Jesus, Ezra, and the angels whom these polytheists worship will not have the power to intercede with God for anyone at the Hour, except for the one who testifies to the truth, who believes in the oneness of God and obeys Him, with a monotheism that he knows and that is true in what His messengers brought.
Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said:

c: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession
, he said: Jesus, Ezra, and the angels. His saying:
h
Except for he who bears witness to the truth
. He said: The word of sincerity, and they know that God is the truth, and Jesus, Ezra, and the angels. He says: Jesus, Ezra, and the angels do not intercede
h
except for he who bears witness to the truth
, and he knows the truth.

x: Others said: What he meant by that is: The gods that the polytheists call upon and worship besides God do not possess intercession except for Jesus, Ezra, their relatives, and the angels who bore witness to the truth and acknowledged it while knowing the truth of what they bore witness to.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession
, except for one who bears witness to the truth and they know: the angels, Jesus, and Ezra, they were worshipped instead of God and they have intercession with God and a status.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except for those who bear witness to the truth. He said: The angels, Jesus, son of Mary, and Ezra, for they have a testimony before God. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God, the Most High, mentioned that those whom the polytheists worship besides God do not have the right to intercede with Him for anyone, except for one who testifies to the truth, and his testimony to the truth is his acknowledgment of the Oneness of God, meaning by that: except for one who believes in God, and they know the reality of His Oneness. He did not specify that the one who does not have the right to intercede among them is some of those who were worshipped besides God. This applies to all of those whom the Quraysh worshipped besides God on the day this verse was revealed, and others besides them. There were among them those who worshipped gods besides God, and there were among them those who worshipped angels and others besides Him. All of them are included in His statement:
h
And those whom the Quraysh and the rest of the Arabs call upon besides God do not have the right to intercede with God

. Then He, the Most High, made an exception by saying: Except for those who bear witness to the truth while they know. They are the ones who bear witness to the truth, and they unify God and sincerely declare His oneness to be sincere, with knowledge and certainty that they possess the power of intercession with Him by His permission for them to do so, as He, the Most High, said: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased.
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 28)
So He, the Most High, confirmed for the angels, Jesus, and Ezra the right to intercession that He denied for the gods and idols by making an exception.

x: God Almighty says: And if you, O Muhammad, ask these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:Who is behind them? They will surely say: God created us. So how are they deluded? So what is the reason for turning them away from worshipping the One who created them, and preventing them from attaining the truth in worshipping Him?
And His statement:
h
And his saying
h
O my Lord
, indeed these are a people who do not believe.' The reciters differed in their reading of His statement:
h
And his saying
. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, and Basra read it <
h
and his saying

>in the accusative case. If it is read in this way, there are two interpretations for it: The first is that it is in apposition to His statement: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? And We hear his saying,
h
O my Lord
. The second is that an accusative is implied for it, so its meaning then is: And his statement:
h
O my Lord
, indeed these are a people who do not believe, and Muhammad complained his complaint to his Lord. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it,
h
and his saying

, in the accusative case, meaning: And with Him is knowledge of the Hour, knowledge of his saying. The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they both have correct meanings.

So whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. So the interpretation of the statement is: And Muhammad said his words, complaining to his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, about his people who denied him, and what he suffered from them: O Lord, these are the ones whom You commanded me to warn and to whom You sent me to call them to You, they are a people who do not believe.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And his saying
h
O my Lord
, these are a people who do not believe.’ He said: So God Almighty confirmed the statement of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And his saying
, ‘O Lord, these are a people who do not believe.’ He said: This is the statement of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, complaining about his people to his Lord.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And his saying
, ‘O Lord,’ he said: It is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, These are people who do not believe.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement: And his saying.
The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, and Basra read it <and his saying>in the accusative case.

If it is read in this way, there are two interpretations for it: The first is that it is in apposition to His statement: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations?
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it, and his saying, in the accusative case, meaning: And with Him is knowledge of the Hour, knowledge of his saying.
The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they both have correct meanings.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in response to his supplication to Him when he said: <O Lord, these are a people who do not believe>so pardon them O Muhammad, and turn away from their harm and say to them “Peace” upon you, and the word “peace” is raised with the pronoun upon you or for you. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement:
h
Then they will know
. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it
h
Then they will know

with a ta’ as a direct address, meaning: God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say that to the polytheists, along with His saying: “Peace.” The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Mecca read it
h
Then they will know
with a ya’ as a statement, and that it is a warning from God to the polytheists. The interpretation of this reading is: So pardon them, O Muhammad, “and say, ‘Peace.’”
Then God Almighty began His warning to them, saying:
h
Then they will know

, what they will encounter of affliction, punishment, and torment for their disbelief. Then God, may He be glorified, abrogated this verse and commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight them.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “So pardon them and say, ‘Peace.’” He said: Pardon them, then he ordered him to fight them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God Almighty said, consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “So pardon them and say, ‘Peace.’ They are going to know.”

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement: Then they will know.

The majority of the reciters of Medina read it Then they will know with a ta’ as a direct address, meaning: God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say that to the polytheists, along with His saying: “Peace.”
The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Mecca read it Then they will know with a ya’ as a statement, and that it is a warning from God to the polytheists.
The interpretation of this reading is: So pardon them, O Muhammad, “and say, ‘Peace.’”
